Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen

主持人先摆出背景：差不多正好三年前，Altman 也被董事会赶下台过；现在网上流传着一封支持黄仁勋的信，主持人认为是照着当年 Altman 的支持者起草的那封信复制粘贴来的。

Altman 说，黄仁勋一直是他心目中的英雄，“英雄也有缺点”。他感激黄仁勋建起的这家公司，对这种处境也有很强的个人共鸣，还记得当时是什么感受，“虽然感觉已经是很久以前的事了”。他说很难想象没有黄仁勋的 AI 革命。英伟达很早就押注了 OpenAI，OpenAI 也很早押注了英伟达，他对此“极其感激”。

主持人接着提到，英伟达为 OpenAI 在俄亥俄州的数据中心提供了最高 1050 亿美元的担保（今年 8 月宣布，担保的是 OpenAI 租用这处数据中心园区的费用）。主持人说英伟达相当于整个行业的“银行”，在给全行业撑腰，并问：这份担保现在还和几周前一样值钱吗？

黄仁勋该不该回来，他在这段采访里没有再回答。

text:
没想到 Jason Wei 已经离开 Meta，去 AI 数据公司 Mercor 当首席科学家

美国时间 11 月 17 日，Mercor CEO Brendan Foody 宣布，Jason Wei 出任首席科学家，负责组建研究团队，主管数据和评测。Jason Wei 随后发帖确认：在 Meta TBD 实验室待了一年，“训练 AI 模型的公司比以往任何时候都多，数据会决定下一个前沿”。

Jason Wei 在 Google Brain 时是思维链论文的第一作者，让模型先写推理步骤再给答案，这个做法后来被广泛使用。之后他在 OpenAI 参与了 o1 和深度研究，2025 年 7 月被 Meta 重金挖走。

他另一个强项是给 AI“出题”。他主导的 SimpleQA 测模型会不会瞎编，BrowseComp 测 AI 能不能翻遍网页找到冷门答案，都成了各家发模型时常用的评测，他还参与了医生打分的 HealthBench。他在博客里写过一条“验证者法则”：一项任务越容易验证，就越容易训练 AI 学会。

Mercor 做的正是这门生意：平台上有 500 多万名医生、律师、工程师，帮 AI 公司出题、写标准答案、给模型打分。11 月 10 日它刚融了 7.5 亿美元，估值 200 亿美元，一年翻倍。现在不只大实验室，越来越多企业拿开源模型自己训练，都需要这类数据和评测。Mercor 10 月起组建研究团队，LoRA 作者 Edward Hu 已经加入。

对 Meta 来说有点尴尬。TBD 实验室由 Scale AI 创始人 Alexandr Wang 领导，Meta 2025 年花 143 亿美元买下 Scale 49% 的股份，而 Mercor 是 Scale 的主要对手。TechCrunch 去年报道，TBD 研究员嫌 Scale 数据质量差，更愿意用 Mercor 和 Surge 的。这也是继 9 月 Andrew Tulloch 被报道转投 Anthropic 之后，TBD 又一位知名研究员离开。

Jason Wei 没说为什么离开 Meta，Meta 暂未回应。

I don't think prompt-injection filtering can be a security boundary for agents on its own. OWASP maps nine dimensions of prompt injection, and a filter tuned for one misses the others, so enforcement has to sit at the action layer.

For each agent-to-tool integration, decide which layers you rely on: input filtering, a logged runtime check per action (allow, ask or block against a declared policy), and a sandbox that limits the damage if the model gets it wrong.

John Schulman and Mark Chen on what research taste is, and how models might learn it:

John: "Research taste is about knowing which ideas are important in the long run, which ideas really catch on and end up going beyond whatever paper they first appear in, but being general and being composable with other ideas."

Mark: "There's taste, which is how you come up with the idea in the first place. The models are still not phenomenally good at taste. They go very deep into things like hyperparameter optimization, essentially tuning all the little knobs that you can tune."

John: "A lot of intuition just comes from personal experience doing research, but to get good at a certain research field, you also have to read a lot of the past work in that field, and you try to absorb the lessons from all this historical work."

"Companies will probably also just do RL from human feedback to collect data from researchers on which proposed ideas are good and which aren't. And that's kind of like absorbing whatever human intuitions the human researchers have developed and trying to bake that into the models."

X AI ALGORITHM UPDATE 🚨

X updated their open source algorithm overnight and copy link is back at 20 points, tied for the biggest number again. Small accounts should focus on: posts people want to send to a friend (so write things worth passing on)

tl;dr:

- in today's release (Nov 18), X's open source code put the score for copying a post's link back to 20
- copy link: 0 → 20
- it sat at 0 for 5 days, from Nov 13
- it's tied with a reply between mutuals for the top spot, and worth about 28 likes
- the "copy link bait" spam check is still in the code
- nothing else moved: likes 0.708, replies 5, DM shares 5

lesson learned: a number that flips twice in a week is a bonus, not a plan

full details:

- The number that came back

On Nov 14 I told you X set copy link to 0. It had been the biggest number since I started reading the code in August.

In today's release it's 20 again.

X didn't say why it went to 0, or why it came back. The code just shows the number.

(I check the open source algo daily with Claude and share updates with you)

- Write it back in

If you crossed copy link off your list after my Nov 14 post, put it back. Yesterday's post called it gone too. As of today, it isn't.

Same deal as always: you hear what the code says the day it says it.

- What a copy link share is

Someone taps share on your post and copies the link, usually to paste it into a group chat, a text or another app.

X guesses how likely each person is to do that. That guess counts 20 again.

- The catch

The "copy link bait" spam check is still there. In the code it adds a spam label to a post, and a spam label keeps a post out of strangers' feeds.

It only shows up in a test, so I can't see if it's running. But begging for link copies is exactly what it's named after.

Posts people want to send on their own are the ones that win.

- My read

20 → 0 → 20 in 5 days. The code doesn't say if that was a test, a mistake or a change of mind, and X may move it again. If it does, I'll tell you.

Meanwhile likes, replies and time spent have only gone one way since October: up.

- What didn't change

Everything else. Likes 0.708, replies 5 (20 between mutuals), DM shares 5, time spent 0.0075. The new multiplying formula from yesterday is still switched off.

Here's a recap of what you should be doing:

- posts people want to pass on, a copied link counts 20 again
- 20 is also what a back and forth with a mutual earns, so follow back your regulars
- sending your post in a DM is worth 5, same as a reply
- likes are at 0.708, the most they've ever counted
- people staying on your post counts more than it did in October
- someone tapping in and staying 10+ seconds adds 0.385
- strangers find you through posts they read all the way through
- under 50K followers, a fresh original can get tried around spot 16
- the likes it gets early on decide which post takes that spot
- that push lasts 2 hours or 200 views, so post when your people are online
- strangers in For You only ever see your originals, never your replies
- every post's first like, then its 32nd, unlocks an extra path to people who don't know you
- one great post beats a pile of okay ones in the same feed
- videos over 10 seconds make the video lists
- in a video the first seconds matter, an open on its own counts 0
- +4 when X thinks a post will earn you a follow
- type your replies yourself, especially under big accounts
- check what your pinned post says about you
- make your profile worth a scroll once someone lands on it

And here's what you should NOT be doing:

- begging for link copies, a "copy link bait" spam check is in the code
- betting everything on copy link, it flipped twice in 5 days
- AI replies under big accounts, X has a flag named "llm slop"
- pasting the same reply everywhere, labeled replies don't reach non-followers' notifications
- tags in a spam-labeled post's photos never notify non-followers
- going after taps, they're down to 0.274
- wandering away from what you're known for, a probable "not interested" knocks off 53.07
- videos people open and close, the open is worth 0
- posting in the middle of the night, the 2 hour push runs out
- thinking replies and reposts reach strangers, they don't
- name-calling, an insult label keeps the post away from non-followers
- getting flagged as misleading or low quality, then strangers see a warning and can't like or share
- 3 adult posts among your last 5 gets your account labeled
- assuming a video passed for good, X looks again once it hits 64 likes and again at 512
- getting your whole account labeled, which cuts you off from strangers
- pinning a link to a site with a bad rating, the label can stick for 7 days
- recycling old posts word for word, X's copypasta check doesn't care that they're yours
- dropping a junk link and tagging people who don't follow you in the same post
- fishing for likes or replies, that label has no exemption even for huge accounts
- posting several in a row, they compete in the same feed
- hashtag piles, none of the 30 scores is about hashtags
- bookmarks for reach, they're not one of the 30
- expecting a 3 day old post in For You, it's out after 2 days

So Diogo Almeida is one of the most fascinating CEOs I have ever interviewed.

born in the Philippines

2008: wins bronze for the Philippines at the International Mathematical Olympiad

2013: starts his career as a software engineer at Amazon

2017: joins Google Brain, working on cutting-edge deep learning research

2018: leaves Google Brain and takes roughly 18 months off to figure out what makes him happy

travels the world, experiments with improv, art and meditation

becomes a top-30 League of Legends player

discovers that none of it makes him particularly happy

2020: joins OpenAI when it's still a relatively obscure research laboratory

helps develop reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), the technique that transforms how people interact with AI

2022: co-authors the landmark InstructGPT paper

the work becomes foundational to ChatGPT

November 2022: ChatGPT launches and becomes one of the fastest-growing consumer products in history

2023: contributes to GPT-4, one of the most important model releases in AI history

but starts questioning the fundamental assumptions behind the technology he helped build

2024: leaves OpenAI while ChatGPT is exploding in popularity

people think he's crazy for walking away

co-founds TypeSafe AI with Erik Gafni and Sasha Sheng

spends two years in stealth developing an entirely new class of AI models

September 15, 2026: launches Jev, TypeSafe's first System One model

Company makes $100M in revenue in the first 7 days of launch

raises a reported $40M seed round led by DCVC

October 2026: a reported $870M Series A at a $7.5B valuation, backed by a16z

argues that the next breakthrough in AI will come from making intelligence cheap, reliable and autonomous

My notes from my discussion with @CompleteSkeptic below:

1. Why Jevons' Paradox Does Not Cut It. We Are Going to 10x That

Diogo expects a "mega Jevons paradox", with usage that dwarfs the token consumption of LLMs and AI running in the background everywhere. He expects people to stop seeing AI as something that "slops crap at them" and start seeing it as something that makes life better.

2. Why SaaS Incumbents Are Better Positioned Than OpenAI and Anthropic in Many Application Spaces

SaaS companies know their customers' workflows and have the scale to fund the upfront engineering that real automation requires. Diogo argues their edge comes from being closest to the problems, not from distribution. Teams inside products like TurboTax know where to improve the interface, while OpenAI and Anthropic are "still living in their ivory tower."

3. Why We Do Not Hire From OpenAI

Diogo sees getting into OpenAI as an anti-signal and says its researchers love algorithms and scaling but hate data. Data is a low-status topic at most labs, and the few people focused on the right task would want to pursue their own. That leaves researchers obsessed with algorithms, which he likens to throwing money in the furnace.

4. How the AI Bubble Could Burst and Where the Demand Shock Could Be

Part of today's AI demand is driven by FOMO, from people believing they are getting good results. Diogo finds many buyers miscalibrated and overestimating what AI can do. Once they face the realities of its capabilities, demand could fall quickly.

5. What Metric Did ChatGPT Optimize for in the Early Days?

Before Claude Code, ChatGPT was optimized for monthly active users rather than the best chatbot experience, which is how sycophancy emerged. Companies are now optimizing for the MAU equivalent in coding agents. Without a dedicated model, Diogo doubts they will produce a comparable one soon.

6. Why the Talent Market Is Not Crazy for Us and We Don't Pay for Mercenaries

TypeSafe pays people good amounts but not the highest, which filters out hired guns. Diogo says Anthropic is suffering from mercenaries because it pays more than anyone else, and an entire market now exists to prepare candidates for Anthropic culture interviews.

7. We Wanted Sonya Huang More Than We Wanted Sequoia

Diogo did not want Sequoia's money and brought the firm in because of Sonya. He values her particular shape of brilliance, which offers a perspective no other advisor gives him. One TypeSafe value is to make great decisions slowly, and he sees her as a valuable thought partner for that.
